summary: Common patterns: all or *, a host, host1:host2 or comma lists, groups, unions, exclusions with !, intersections with &, combinations, and wildcards on FQDNs or IPs mixed with groups. Commas are preferred for ranges and IPv6.
questions: How do I target hosts in one group but not another?
How do I target hosts that are in both webservers and staging?
Can I use wildcards in host patterns?
Should I use commas or colons in host lists?

answer_card.title: Common host patterns
answer_card.answer_md:
| Target | Pattern |
|---|---|
| All hosts | `all` or `*` |
| One host | `host1` |
| Several hosts | `host1:host2` or `host1,host2` |
| Union of groups | `webservers:dbservers` |
| Exclude | `webservers:!atlanta` |
| Intersection | `webservers:&staging` |

Combine: `webservers:dbservers:&staging:!phoenix`. Wildcards work if hosts are named by FQDN/IP: `192.0.*`, `*.example.com`, `one*.com:dbservers`. Prefer commas with ranges and IPv6.
